newsitem.title: UK: British Energy to cut jobs, make savings.
newsitem.headline: British Energy to cut jobs, make savings.

text.p: British nuclear electricity generator British Energy Plc said on Wednesday it expected to cut 1,460 jobs within the next three years to achieve annual savings of 50 million pounds ($78.11 million) a year in staff costs.

It said the plans, in line with commitments made at privatisation, would see a one-off restructuring cost of 100 million pounds which is fully covered by existing provisions, spread over three financial years.
"We will continue to drive to reduce costs and improve overall efficiency to ensure we are competitive," chief executive Robert Hawley said in a statement.

British Energy shares were up half a penny at 108 pence, fractionally above its part-paid flotation price of 105 pence for institutions, after the announcement, which detailed job losses of 1,200 in Nuclear Electric and 260 at Scottish Nuclear.

The company was one of the most unpopular of the ruling Conservative Party's flotations when it was sold in July this year and has already met fierce criticism for the plans, after they were widely flagged in newspaper reports earlier this week.

Unions have expressed concern that the job cuts could affect safety at the company's eight nuclear power stations, but Hawley said the redundancies would be "against a background of never compromising on our total commitment to safety."
